clue.text: Guide to making food in English clubs ready to eat outside

indicators.note: something placed outside another wraps around it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: fruit ready to eat is ripe
standard abbreviation for English
C is the abbreviation for the card suit clubs

explanation.surface: A culinary guide set in English clubs, where the food is served ready to eat outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The ripe fruit sits outside the pair of abbreviations: R(EC)IPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of instructions for preparing a dish, literally a guide for cooks.

clue.text: Leaders I frantically got ready for

indicators.note: acting frantically means flailing about wildly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Political leaders, with the speaker, hurriedly prepared for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' is slang for cash, so to get ready for something is to sell it for money, which is to realise it.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an asset is to convert it into cash, and 'ready' is old slang for money.

clue.text: In time, get on board lots of fish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to reach a train or bus before it leaves and board it
second meaning: the haul an angler or trawler brings in

explanation.surface: A fisherman hurrying to get aboard a boat loaded with fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a whole phrase: you catch a bus when you get on it in time.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to board transport before it departs; the noun is the quantity of fish landed.

clue.text: Massive monument English queen in decline set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it, so the letters read from bottom to top
one thing sitting in another means it is enclosed by it

parts.note: a dip is a fall or decline
Mary I and Mary II were queens of England

explanation.surface: A great monument to an English queen whose reign was in decline is erected.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen goes inside the dip to make DI(MARY)P, and the whole is then turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian pyramids are among the most massive monuments ever built, tombs for pharaohs.

clue.text: State in which you'll find 50% of Alaskans — plus earlier 25%

indicators.note: only half of the word survives, the opening half being dropped
a further quarter of the same word is kept, the stretch coming just before the half already taken

parts.note: taken as written, then trimmed to its second half
the same word again, trimmed to its second quarter

explanation.surface: A trivia-style claim about one US state's share of Alaskan residents.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word into quarters AL, AS, KA, NS; take the last half, then add the quarter preceding it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest.

clue.text: For example, a story in newspaper

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a part of speech, of which 'a' is an instance
second meaning: a piece of journalism

explanation.surface: Offering one newspaper story as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is not a filler word here: it is itself the indefinite one in grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'a' and 'the' are this word class; in journalism it names a written piece in a paper.

clue.text: Small brat revealed to be fool

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a mischievous child
to let on is to disclose

explanation.surface: A little brat turns out to be an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish, gullible person, a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Standing of University shown in facts and figures

indicators.note: being shown in something places it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: informal short form of statistics
standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A university's reputation as reflected in league-table data.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's rank or position in society, synonymous with standing.

clue.text: One appears in improper cabaret, cause of some complaints

indicators.note: appearing in something means being found inside it
improper means not in the proper form, so the letters are out of their right order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A performer turns up in a risqué cabaret show that prompts complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaints' is meant in the medical sense of ailments, not grumbles about the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are microbes behind many illnesses, which are informally called complaints.

clue.text: Caught in middle of change, quarrel

indicators.note: placed in the middle of a word, a letter is inserted at its centre

parts.note: a change or modification
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone caught amid a period of change ends up in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy argument or dispute, a synonym for quarrel.

clue.text: Amorous male precisely interrupted by person in charge of event

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing break into its middle

parts.note: the idiom 'to a T' means exactly
master of ceremonies

explanation.surface: A lovelorn man is cut off mid-sentence by the event's host.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomcat is a male cat, and the word is also slang for a womaniser who prowls for partners.

clue.text: Hard piece of advice taken wrong way, in essence

indicators.note: going the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the letters are read right to left

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
a tip is a helpful hint

explanation.surface: Tough advice that someone has misunderstood, at its core.
explanation.definitionFit: Pith is the core or central substance of a matter, as in a pithy remark.

clue.text: Sorted clues out — I'm extremely careful

indicators.note: sorting things puts them into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A crossword solver boasts of having worked out every clue with great care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of the phrase 'sorted out', but its letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail, thoroughly precise.

clue.text: Speculation about less civilised people creating state of confusion

indicators.note: something put about another surrounds it on both sides

parts.note: a bet is a speculative wager
comparative of wild, untamed
men are people

explanation.surface: Guesswork about uncivilised tribes that leaves everyone baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewilderment is the condition of being puzzled and perplexed.

clue.text: I arranged concert about right? Wrong

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it
arranged means set out afresh, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A promoter wonders whether they organised a concert properly, and decides they didn't.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged concert letters go round the single right letter, all after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorrect means not true or accurate, a direct synonym for wrong.

clue.text: Guerrilla taking power, supported by skilled worker

indicators.note: in a down clue, being supported by something means sitting on top of it

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
a craftsman

explanation.surface: An irregular fighter seizes power, backed by a craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Partisans are irregular resistance fighters operating behind enemy lines, the same as guerrillas.

clue.text: Steps down from deck using method following mate

indicators.note: coming after another word, this piece is placed second

parts.note: a mate is a friend
a way of doing something

explanation.surface: A sailor descends from the deck in the manner of a ship's mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' suggests a ship's officer, but here it simply means a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, a companionway is the staircase or ladder leading below from the deck.

clue.text: Brings up issue as female, partly from other standpoint

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone raises a matter as a woman, viewing it from a different angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means children, not a topic, so the definition is raising offspring as a woman does.
explanation.definitionFit: To mother is to rear children; issue is a legal word for offspring.

clue.text: How halves of seesaw differ, with extreme force

definitions.note: a phrase, read as two words IN TENSE
definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two: 'see' is present and 'saw' past, a difference of grammatical time
second meaning: very strong or powerful

explanation.walkthrough: The playground toy is a red herring; its two halves are verbs, one present and one past.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means of great strength or degree; split as two words it says where see and saw differ.

clue.text: I'm appearing in something stunning, Asian garment

indicators.note: being in something means being placed inside it

parts.note: a knockout stuns an opponent
taken as written
a performer who is on is appearing on stage

explanation.surface: A model announces she's wearing a dazzling outfit from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing' is the theatrical sense, a performer being on stage; 'stunning' means knocking out, not dazzling.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is the traditional long robe of Japan, a garment from Asia.

clue.text: Author of book, novel bitter in inclination

indicators.note: being in something places it inside

parts.note: a ship's list is its lean or tilt

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer of a book, leaning towards a bitter novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' here is the text of an opera or musical, and 'novel' is the anagram signal, not a work of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A librettist writes the libretto, the words of an opera, which theatre people call its book.

clue.text: Save last of port in cask

parts.note: save and but both mean except

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Keep the dregs of the port in the barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A butt is a large barrel for wine or ale, a kind of cask.

clue.text: Bust ringleader imprisoned by magistrate

indicators.note: something imprisoned is shut inside another thing

parts.note: beak is British slang for a magistrate or judge
read as the leader of 'ring', its first letter

explanation.surface: A gang's ringleader, having been nicked, is jailed by the magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' must be split: the leader of 'ring'. 'Bust' looks like an arrest, but it is the definition as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bust something is to break it, informally; both mean to smash or ruin.

clue.text: Stick together in company at this point

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
here means at this place

explanation.surface: Colleagues told to stay united as a firm at this moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together firmly as a unified whole.

clue.text: Negative response to various points repeatedly seen as rubbish

parts.note: a refusal
three compass points: north, south, east
the same compass points again

explanation.surface: Repeatedly saying no to several arguments is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' are compass points; 'repeatedly' asks for the same set twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense means foolish talk or ideas, the same as rubbish used figuratively.

clue.text: Start off job with little time to exercise? That's stupid

indicators.note: with its start taken off, a word loses its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written, then cut
T is the abbreviation for time
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: Quitting work to have a little time for the gym seems dumb.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow to understand, mentally dull, a synonym of stupid.

clue.text: Yank wearing old jacket

parts.note: to yank is to pull sharply
dressed in something

explanation.surface: An American dressed in a vintage coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is a verb meaning tug.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a close-fitting sleeveless jacket, historically of leather, worn in earlier centuries.
